title: Anthropic IPO docs reportedly reveal over $40B in losses last year
content:
Anthropic IPO docs reportedly reveal over $40 billion in losses last year
Anthropic, one of the biggest AI companies in the world, is currently gearing up to go public. As the Claude-maker prepares for a potential blockbuster IPO later this year, Reuters has got its hands on the company's prospectus, which lays out Anthropic's financials and risks for investors.
According to the prospectus obtained by Reuters, Anthropic made $4.6 billion in revenue in 2025. That's twelve times its growth in the previous year.
But there's bad news, too: The AI company lost more than it brought in last year, Reuters reported. A lot more.

Anthropic reportedly lost a whopping $42 billion in 2025. Of that net loss, $8.06 billion was spent on operating costs in 2025, far higher than its 2024 operating costs of $2.98 billion, according to Reuters. In addition, the documents Reuters reviewed stated that compute and infrastructure costs from Anthropic's AI lab amounted to an additional $7.33 billion.
Anthropic is hardly alone in spending more than it takes in, however. In July, after pouring money into AI development, Google reported its first quarter of negative cash flow since the company went public.
The AI industry is in the midst of a massive infrastructure build-out, with an estimated trillion dollars being spent on AI data centers, energy, and other resources in 2026 alone. Axios recently reported that the industry as a whole is expected to spend $10 trillion through 2032.
So, it's hardly surprising that Reuters reported that Anthropic's capital expenditures will only balloon in the years ahead. The IPO prospectus seen by Reuters stated that the company plans to spend $518 billion on "cloud, computing and infrastructure obligations" over the next few years. To make matters even more concerning for potential investors, about 80 percent of that $518 billion is allocated to non-cancelable deals.
Anthropic is currently eyeing a public offering that would put the company at a $2 trillion valuation.
Topics Artificial Intelligence Anthropic

report.summary: Reuters reports Anthropic's IPO prospectus shows $4.6B 2025 revenue but a $42B net loss, as AI infrastructure costs surge ahead of a possible $2T listing.
report.background: Anthropic, maker of Claude, is preparing for a blockbuster IPO. Reuters obtained the company's prospectus, which reveals financials and risks for investors. The reported loss reflects industry-wide economics: frontier model training and inference require massive compute, data centers, energy, and talent. Revenue is growing fast—12x to $4.6 billion—but costs far exceed it. Google recently reported its first negative cash flow quarter since going public, and the AI sector is expected to spend trillions on infrastructure. Investors must weigh hypergrowth against enormous capital intensity. Anthropic reportedly plans $518 billion in cloud, computing, and infrastructure obligations, about 80% non-cancelable, while eyeing a $2 trillion valuation. The tension: AI firms must spend ahead of revenue, betting scale leads to future profits, but public markets may demand a clearer path.
key_points: Anthropic reportedly earned $4.6 billion in 2025 revenue, twelve times its prior-year growth, but posted a $42 billion net loss. Operating costs rose to $8.06 billion from $2.98 billion, and compute/infrastructure added $7.33 billion. The gap illustrates how aggressively the company is spending to train and run Claude while chasing market share.

The filing comes as Anthropic prepares to go public at a reported $2 trillion valuation. Reuters reviewed the prospectus, which outlines financials and risks. If accurate, the scale of losses may test public investor appetite, especially because the company plans $518 billion in cloud, computing, and infrastructure obligations, about 80% non-cancelable.

Anthropic is not alone. Google reported its first negative cash flow quarter since going public after heavy AI investment. The sector is building massive data centers, energy capacity, and chips, with estimates of $1 trillion in 2026 and $10 trillion through 2032. This suggests AI profits may remain distant as capital expenditures escalate.

The prospectus reportedly flags ballooning capital expenditures. Non-cancelable deals mean Anthropic must pay even if demand slows. Public investors will weigh hypergrowth against huge fixed costs, potential margin pressure, and competition from OpenAI, Google, Meta, and others. The IPO could become a referendum on whether frontier AI business models can eventually deliver returns.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Anthropic's reported losses underscore that even top labs are burning cash at unprecedented scale, reinforcing a compute arms race. Developers may benefit from continued model improvements and API competition, but pricing could rise if investors demand profitability. Cloud providers and chipmakers remain key winners. For regular users, Claude and similar tools may stay cheap or bundled in the near term, but long-term access could depend on sustainable monetization. Public markets may become more skeptical of AI startups with heavy losses, affecting funding, hiring, and open-source alternatives.
report.tools: To follow Anthropic's IPO and AI economics, watch SEC EDGAR for filings, Reuters and Bloomberg for prospectus reporting, and OpenBB for open-source financial analysis. Epoch AI tracks compute trends and model costs; Crunchbase and PitchBook cover private funding. For LLM cost tracking, Langfuse and Helicone help developers monitor API spend. These tools can help contextualize whether AI infrastructure spending translates into sustainable revenue.
